title: IANUS: Integrated Accelerator based on NPU-PIM Unified Memory System
problem: End-to-end LLM inference has diverse compute characteristics that challenge previous accelerators, which only address specific operations or stages (e.g., self-attention or generation). A unified system must efficiently handle both computation-heavy and memory-intensive workloads.
motivation: Accelerating end-to-end transformer-based LLM inference is critical for AI services in datacenters.
method: IANUS combines a Neural Processing Unit (NPU) with Processing-in-Memory (PIM) in a unified main memory system where PIM memory serves as both computational substrate and NPU main memory. Novel PIM Access Scheduling manages scheduling of normal memory accesses and PIM computations while mapping workloads across NPU and PIM, addressing the constraint that memory accesses and PIM operations cannot happen simultaneously.
key_novelty: Unified main memory architecture where PIM serves both as computational accelerator and shared memory for the NPU, with coordinated access scheduling to minimize data movement.
contributions: Domain-specific heterogeneous architecture combining NPU and PIM for end-to-end LLM inference acceleration
PIM Access Scheduling algorithm for coordinating memory accesses, PIM computations, and workload distribution
6.2x speedup over NVIDIA A100 GPU on GPT-2 inference
Prototype implementation with commercial PIM, NPU, and FPGA-based controller demonstrating feasibility

metrics.speedup: 6.2x vs NVIDIA A100 GPU; 3.2x vs state-of-the-art accelerator on GPT-2

primary_theme: LLM inference acceleration via NPU-PIM unified heterogeneous system
